_README: The closed-test roster. mint_tester_pins.py and tester_status.py BOTH
read this file, so there is one list instead of two that drift.
To add a tester: add a line to 'testers' with their gmail and the demo
flat they log in with, then add the same address to the Play Console
tester list (Testers tab). Both are needed -- the Play list decides who
CAN install, this file decides who gets a PIN.
Two testers may share a flat. It works, but a login timestamp then
cannot tell them apart, and PIN lockout is per flat -- five wrong
attempts locks BOTH of them out for ten minutes. Prefer one flat each.
reviewer_flat is Google's reviewer. It must never appear in 'testers':
its PIN went into App Access before rollout, and re-minting it would
hand the reviewer a login that fails.
opted_on: set this to the date (YYYY-MM-DD) a tester CONFIRMS they
pressed 'Become a tester'. It matters most on a shared flat: a login
there proves ONE of the two opted in and cannot say which, so without
this field the count would credit both and overstate your progress.
PLAY CONSOLE IS A THIRD LIST, 7 Oct. This file and the Play Console email
list drifted apart in BOTH directions and nothing compared them. Three
testers here were never on the Play list and could not opt in however long
they were chased; one address on the Play list
(saswatiiiparida05@gmail.com) has no flat here and could opt in but not
log in. Before chasing anyone, compare the two lists.
A tester needs THREE things and the absence of any one is silent:
1. on the Play Console email list   -> can opt in
2. a row in 'testers' below         -> gets a PIN
3. an ANDROID phone                 -> can INSTALL and USE it
device: android | ios | unknown. Opting in does NOT prove android --
the opt-in page is a Google-account action in a browser, so an iPhone
owner can press 'Become a tester' and then never install anything. That
is the worst case for this test, because it counts toward the twelve
while contributing no usage, and Google looks at both.
One PERSON, not one address. Two accounts belonging to the same person on
the same handset are one tester, whatever the list says. Confirmed 8 Oct:
akash08bhardwaj and aakash.aakashb.bhardwaj are both Akash;
saswatiiiparida05 and saswatiiparida6 are both Saswati. So the Play Console
list of 15 addresses is 13 people, and 4 of those are on iPhones.
saswatiiiparida05 is deliberately NOT given a flat. It is Saswati's second
address on Saswati's phone; a flat for it would be padding, and padding is
the small version of the thing that gets a developer account terminated.
_dropped records who was removed and why, so nobody re-adds them.
FLAT SUPPLY, 5 Oct: the society was grown from eight populated flats to
fifteen. seed_gate.py now seeds C-101 (which had been created by hand and
was empty) plus A-302, B-108, B-210, C-304, D-205 and D-410, each with an
owner, a registered vehicle and gate history.
A flat MUST be in seed_gate.DEMO_FLATS before a tester is given it.
mint_tester_pins.py refuses otherwise. A flat the seeder does not know
about has no owner, no vehicle and no gate history, so the tester logs in
successfully and sees an empty app -- which reads as a broken app.
Sharing a flat is now unnecessary for new testers and there are spare
flats. The five existing shared pairs were left alone deliberately: moving
someone to a new flat means minting a new PIN and re-sending their message,
and two of them are already opted in with the fourteen-day clock running.
The cost of leaving them is that last_seen is per flat, so on a shared flat
it cannot say WHICH of the two opened the app.
